transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-08-05
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Raman (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (Solaris Head of ML), Marco Diaz (Solaris Platform Eng), Sophie Lin (Solaris Product), Ethan Park (CTO)
---
[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh quick intro. I'm Jordan, AE at Redwood, and with me is Priya, our SE. How's everyone doing?
[00:12] Aisha Khan: Good, thanks. Ready to see what you have around evals.
[00:16] Priya Raman: Awesome, we'll show the Console eval and quality monitoring flows, plus the API for programmatic runs. We'll try to keep it practical for your clinical summarization use case.
[00:28] Ethan Park: Great, we only have 40 minutes so please be concise.
[00:32] Jordan Lee: Totally. Quick agenda, we'll cover prompt sets and labeling, regression alerts, A/B comparisons and dashboards, then Q&A and next steps.
[01:05] Priya Raman: Jumping in—opening the Redwood Console. First is the prompt sets page, you can import CSVs or integrate via API. We typically recommend starting with a stratified prompt set that reflects patient notes, varying length and modality.
[01:28] Sophie Lin: When you say stratified, do you mean by doc type and length?
[01:33] Priya Raman: Yeah, exactly, like discharge summaries vs progress notes. Also include edge cases that tend to break the model.
[01:47] Marco Diaz: Are prompt sets stored in our account or in Redwood? How long are they retained?
[01:52] Jordan Lee: Good question—by default prompt sets are stored in the customer namespace on Redwood's control plane so you can version them; retention is configurable, and we can support retention policies for pilot accounts.
[02:10] Aisha Khan: We need data residency guarantees and audit logs for anything that might contain PHI.
[02:16] Priya Raman: Understood. For Private deployments you can keep the control plane in your VPC, and we have KMS integrations and audit logs. For hosted, we provide SOC 2 controls and retention options; we'll share the security doc.
[02:40] Jordan Lee: I'll attach the security pack after the call. Regarding evals—here's an example prompt set with human references for quality scoring. You can run automated scorers or upload human labels.
[03:05] [INTERVAL - SCREEN SHARING - Dashboard loads slowly]
[03:20] Priya Raman: This is the A/B comparison view—you can compare model A (open-llm-13b) vs model B (redwood-verified-13b-quant) across metrics like ROUGE, BLEU, and custom clinical F1. We support custom metric plugins.
[03:46] Marco Diaz: Can we plug in our internal metric? We have a clinical concept overlap score.
[03:50] Priya Raman: Yes, you can add a custom metric via the SDK or a webhook. We'll share the sample plugin.
[04:07] Sophie Lin: How are regression alerts defined? Are they per-prompt-set or global?
[04:14] Priya Raman: Alerts can be scoped per-prompt-set, per-model, or across a route. You set thresholds and baselines—if metric delta exceeds the threshold we trigger alerts and can auto-create an issue in Jira or Slack.
[04:36] Ethan Park: We want to get alerted on clinically meaningful regressions only, to avoid noise.
[04:42] Priya Raman: Totally—you can tune sensitivity, and there's a noise-filtering feature that looks for statistically significant changes over a moving window.
[05:05] [00:05 - small crosstalk, typing]
[05:20] Aisha Khan: For A/B, do you do online traffic splits or offline eval?
[05:25] Priya Raman: Both. Offline A/Bs are run on prompt sets; online A/Bs can be routed via the Redwood API with traffic splits—you get per-split metrics and the compare view aggregates them.
[05:44] Jordan Lee: Important note—online A/Bs will consume tokens from whichever model endpoints you route to, so cost accounting is per-split.
[06:01] Marco Diaz: What's the latency overhead for the eval pipeline? If we sample production traffic and run evals, will it add latency to the user path?
[06:09] Priya Raman: We never inject eval work into the critical path; sampling is asynchronous. For synchronous scoring on-the-fly you can use the lightweight scorer that runs in-proc, but we recommend async to avoid tail latency impact.
[06:30] [00:10 - brief pause]
[06:42] Sophie Lin: How does this integrate with our CI for model rollouts? We want pre-deploy checks.
[06:48] Priya Raman: You can run evals as part of the CI by calling the Redwood Eval API in a job, then gate a rollout based on thresholds. We also have canary rollouts in Console.
[07:10] Jordan Lee: Let's show a regression alert example—Priya, can you open the Alerts page?
[07:18] Priya Raman: Sure, here's a recent regression alert we simulated—metric delta on clinical F1 dropped by 6% for the cardiology subset. You can click to see failing prompts, diffs between model outputs, and operator notes.
[07:40] Marco Diaz: That failing prompt list looks useful. Is the diff human-readable or token-level?
[07:46] Priya Raman: Human-readable with colorized highlights for insertions/deletions; you can switch to token-level if you want.
[08:05] Aisha Khan: About privacy—are failing prompts stored in plaintext in your UI? We need to mask PHI.
[08:12] Priya Raman: We support redaction rules and can mask or tokenize PHI before storing in the control plane. For Private/On-prem deployments you can keep everything inside your VPC.
[08:30] Jordan Lee: Also we have an option to store only embeddings/hashes for diagnostics if full text isn't allowed.
[08:45] [00:04 - brief interruption, someone grabs coffee]
[09:00] Sophie Lin: On A/B comparisons—do you support confidence intervals and statistical testing?
[09:06] Priya Raman: Yes, we compute bootstrap CIs and run paired significance tests; you can select the test and alpha level.
[09:20] Ethan Park: How do you handle model variants and quantized forks? For example, we'd like to compare a 4-bit quant vs float for cost/latency tradeoffs.
[09:29] Priya Raman: We track model variants; the model catalog shows verified performance profiles and we surface quantization tradeoffs. You can do side-by-side cost vs quality plots.
[09:44] Marco Diaz: Can Redwood run the evals against our private models if we self-host?
[09:50] Priya Raman: Yes—if you're on Redwood Private or have a Private control plane we can run evals against models in your network. For on-prem you can run the Eval worker inside your infra.
[10:12] Jordan Lee: Quick aside—what's your timeline for selecting a solution?
[10:16] Aisha Khan: We're hoping to decide by end of August and run a 4-week pilot in September.
[10:23] Jordan Lee: That fits a typical cadence. We'll propose a pilot SOW for the 4-week evaluation focusing on summary quality and regression monitoring.
[10:36] [00:15 - screen scroll, demo lags]
[11:00] Priya Raman: Walking through the prompt set import—CSV columns: prompt_id, prompt_text, reference, label, cohort_tag. You can also upload JSONL. We auto-detect columns but include a mapping step.
[11:24] Sophie Lin: Can we version prompt sets? We need to track changes over time.
[11:28] Priya Raman: Yes, prompt sets are versioned and you can diff versions to see what changed. That helps explain drift.
[11:45] Marco Diaz: For alerts, can we route to our incident system? We use PagerDuty.
[11:50] Jordan Lee: We have built-in integrations with Slack, Jira, PagerDuty and webhooks.
[12:05] Aisha Khan: A quick security question—do you support SAML SSO and SCIM?
[12:10] Jordan Lee: Yes, SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning; we also support RBAC and org roles.
[12:22] Ethan Park: KMS integrations for key rotation?
[12:26] Priya Raman: We integrate with AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and customer HSMs for Private deployments.
[12:40] [00:05 - note-taking sound]
[12:52] Sophie Lin: Regarding false positives in regression alerts—what's the recommended approach to tune?
[12:58] Priya Raman: Start with higher thresholds on sensitive cohorts, use the moving window significance test, and whitelist known noisy prompts. We can also run a calibration period to estimate typical variance.
[13:20] Marco Diaz: How heavy is the compute for re-running evals? If we do daily runs over 10k prompts, cost might add up.
[13:28] Priya Raman: Costs depend on model size and run frequency. Redwood Optimize suggests batching and quantization profiles to reduce per-token cost; offline evals can be scheduled during off-peak to exploit lower rates on Dedicated.
[13:50] Jordan Lee: We'll include cost estimates in the pilot proposal using your dataset size and targeted sampling rate.
[14:05] [00:20 - brief lunch scheduling chatter unrelated]
[14:30] Priya Raman: Demoing the alert detail—here's the failing prompt, model outputs side-by-side, and the human label. You can annotate directly in the UI and push annotations back into training or the prompt set.
[14:56] Aisha Khan: Push to training—do you have connectors to our MLOps pipeline?
[15:01] Priya Raman: We have connectors for common pipelines (Airflow, MLflow) and webhooks to trigger retrain jobs. We'll share example playbooks.
[15:20] Marco Diaz: One concern—if we use hosted Redwood to run evals on PHI, will that complicate our compliance?
[15:27] Jordan Lee: It can. For PHI we recommend Private deployment or the on-prem eval worker. For hosted we offer redaction and limited retention, but we understand your compliance bar may require Private.
[15:46] Sophie Lin: What's the minimal dataset to get reliable alerts?
[15:51] Priya Raman: It varies by cohort; for common metrics we recommend several hundred labeled examples per cohort for initial sensitivity. For rarer events we use stratified sampling and bootstrap techniques.
[16:10] [00:10 - brief pause]
[16:35] Jordan Lee: Quick note on APIs—we have Eval API endpoints to run single prompts, batch runs, and to upload labels. SDKs in Python and Node.
[16:48] Aisha Khan: Can we automate our own CI to call the SDK and gate a PR?
[16:52] Priya Raman: Yes, customers integrate eval calls into CI; we provide examples in the repo.
[17:10] Marco Diaz: Any limitations around sequence length or tokenization that affect scoring?
[17:16] Priya Raman: Scorers accept model outputs and references; if you have long clinical notes, we'll chunk with overlap or score summaries. The runtime supports long context models and KV cache optimizations but scoring pipelines may need chunk-aware metrics.
[17:44] Sophie Lin: Could you show the A/B chart comparing quality vs cost?
[17:48] [SCREEN - chart loads, small lag]
[18:05] Priya Raman: Here's cost-quality scatter—each point is a model variant; we overlay throughput and latency bands. You can filter by cohort.
[18:26] Ethan Park: That visualization will help us with exec buy-in.
[18:30] Jordan Lee: We'll export these charts to PDF for the pilot report.
[18:42] [00:10 - background typing]
[19:00] Aisha Khan: On the pilot, can we scope it to cardiology and neurology summaries?
[19:05] Jordan Lee: Yes, we can scope cohorts. Pilot deliverables typically include baseline eval, configured alerts, and a go/no-go recommendation.
[19:20] Marco Diaz: What about model hosting? We might want to use our own fine-tuned models on Dedicated.
[19:26] Priya Raman: Dedicated supports customer model builds; you can bring your model image or use Redwood-managed model hosting with private model access.
[19:44] Sophie Lin: How do we track prompt set drift over time in the UI?
[19:49] Priya Raman: There's a drift tab that shows distribution shifts in prompt length, token distribution, and cohort prevalence, with automatic alerting.
[20:10] [00:15 - small cross-talk]
[20:40] Jordan Lee: Ok, quick recap: we'll send pilot SOW, security docs, and the eval guide. Priya will share sample prompt set CSV and plugin examples. Marco will provide sample prompts and logs for cost estimate.
[21:05] Aisha Khan: We'll aim to have the sample dataset to you by 2025-08-12.
[21:12] Jordan Lee: Great—anything else on requirements?
[21:20] Ethan Park: Two final items: one, we need a KMS/SSO checklist; two, please outline the Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs and cost buckets.
[21:33] Jordan Lee: We'll include both in the follow-up.
[21:40] [00:20 - demo wrap up, links posted in chat]
[22:05] Priya Raman: Sharing links—eval guide doc, sample prompt set CSV, plugin example repo. Also pushing a demo recording.
[22:20] Sophie Lin: Thanks, that was helpful.
[22:24] Marco Diaz: Quick question—do you have an API quota model for evals?
[22:30] Jordan Lee: Yes, eval runs consume tokens and are billed; for pilots we often offer trial credits and an agreed cap.
[22:45] Aisha Khan: Ok, appreciate it.
[23:05] [00:30 - small chat about follow-up times]
[23:40] Jordan Lee: Final next steps—Jordan to send SOW and pricing by Friday the 8th, Priya to share artifacts by Thursday the 7th, Solaris to provide sample prompts by the 12th. We'll schedule the technical POC the week of Aug 18th.
[24:00] Ethan Park: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[24:05] [MEETING ENDS - total duration ~42m; timestamps in transcript approximate]
